Xiao Yu silently swept the fallen leaves in front of the woodshed, while several disciples gathered not far away, pointing at him without restraint.  

"Is this the same Xiao Yu who claimed to be the top disciple of the Mad Blade Sect? How did he end up living in the woodshed?"  

"You didn't know? He practiced some dark arts, messed up his qi, and now he’s just a cripple!"  

"I always said it—a bastard with no parents, joining our sect and becoming so strong in such a short time? Clearly, he took the wrong path! Disgrace to the Mad Blade Sect!"  

Xiao Yu cast a cold glance at them, his former aura of dominance still lingering enough to silence the cowards. Just as he lowered his head to resume his work, another unwelcome voice rang out:  

"Hmph, a broken-toothed cur still putting on airs and bullying fellow disciples?"  

The speaker was none other than Song Baishu, the senior disciple of the Mad Blade Sect. The sycophants immediately flocked to him, spewing flattery. Xiao Yu remained indifferent, continuing to sweep.  

Song Baishu sneered. "You dare not greet your senior when he arrives?"  

Xiao Yu replied coldly, "We are both disciples of the sect, equals. Besides, I’ve been expelled. Why should I bow to you?"  

In a flash, Song Baishu lunged, grabbing Xiao Yu’s face and slamming his head into the ground. Blood gushed from Xiao Yu’s orifices, a gruesome sight.  

"You think you can lecture me, cripple?"  

Song Baishu wiped his hand with a handkerchief before stepping on Xiao Yu’s head as if he were a stray dog. Barely conscious, Xiao Yu spat a mouthful of blood onto Song Baishu’s face and laughed wildly.  

Enraged, Song Baishu was about to finish him off when a graceful figure rushed in—Wang Xun’er, the Sect Master’s daughter, who had been out buying medicine for Xiao Yu.  

"Junior Sister, why protect this traitor?"  

Wang Xun’er helped Xiao Yu up, her eyes blazing. "Xiao Yu and I are betrothed. If you harm him again, don’t blame me for being ruthless!"  

Song Baishu scowled. "The Sect Master annulled that engagement. Why cling to this cripple? I’ll ask for your hand myself!"  

As he spoke, he suddenly struck, aiming to knock her out. Xiao Yu, though powerless, still had sharp eyes and warned her just in time.  

Song Baishu dropped all pretense. "Xiao Yu altered the Mad Blade techniques and leaked them! The Sect Master ordered his death. Why defy it?"  

Xiao Yu frowned—when had he done such a thing? Ignoring the accusation, Wang Xun’er grabbed his hand and fled toward the back mountain. Pursuers swarmed after them, and though they held back to avoid harming the Sect Master’s daughter, both were soon wounded.  

At the cliff’s edge, Xiao Yu looked at Wang Xun’er, guilt and pain in his eyes.  

"This is far enough."  

Before she could react, he leaped. In his final moments, he realized the truth—his shattered meridians were the Sect Master’s doing. He had honestly pointed out flaws in the Mad Blade techniques, only to be betrayed.  

The Mad Blade Sect wasn’t worthy of him. If reborn, he’d show that stagnant Sect Master what true martial arts were!  

---  

After Xiao Yu’s fall, Sect Master Wang tried to wed Xun’er to Song Baishu, but she refused. With the Sect Master aging, power gradually shifted to Song Baishu, who, once obsessed with surpassing Xiao Yu, now found the sect’s teachings lackluster. He neglected training, indulged in luxury, and even berated the old Sect Master as a "stubborn failure."  

Three years later, a straw-sandaled youth arrived, challenging the sect. The disciples, thinking him weak, attacked—only to be swiftly defeated.  

To make matters worse, the rival Divine Sword Sect seized the chance to humiliate the Mad Blade Sect. Song Baishu fought but, lacking true mastery, was disarmed and nearly killed.  

The straw-sandaled youth intervened, then demonstrated the Mad Blade techniques with such power that the Divine Sword expert conceded defeat.  

As Song Baishu crawled to thank him, another figure appeared. The youth brightened, calling out, "Master!"  

The newcomer was Xiao Yu, who had survived the fall, restored his meridians, and taken the youth—a former beggar—as his disciple.  

Xiao Yu had no interest in revenge; he’d come only for Wang Xun’er. The broken Song Baishu could only kneel in bitter recognition.  

The old Sect Master wept, regretting his past folly. But Xiao Yu had moved on. With Wang Xun’er and his disciples, he wandered the land, righting wrongs until his name echoed across the realm.
